Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Denver/Boulder CO
144 PM MDT Tue Oct 13 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Much cooler temperatures and wet conditions is still on track.

- Rain and mountain snow showers will become more numerous
  tonight, mainly west of I-25. More widespread rain and mountain
  snow still on schedule for Wednesday afternoon - Wednesday 
  night, before winding down Thursday. 

- Several inches (6-12") of snow expected for the mountains above
  9,000 to 10,000 feet with travel impacts late Wednesday thru 
  Thursday morning. Lighter snow and at least a dusting into the 
  mountain valleys and higher foothills. 

- Drier and warmer again for next weekend. 

&&

.DISCUSSION /Through Tuesday/...
Issued at 144 PM MDT Tue Oct 13 2026

Satellite imagery shows the upper level low diving southeast 
across Nevada. The low will bottom out over northern Arizona 
tonight and be centered over the Four Corners 18Z Wednesday. Water
vapor imagery and radar show an area of lift over eastern Utah 
and western Colorado, with widespread showers. This area of lift 
shifts eastward tonight bringing rain and mountain snow showers to
the western two-thirds of Colorado. Easterly low level flow will 
continue tonight and Wednesday around the low to our southwest and
a surface high to the north. Cross sections show that the low 
levels will become saturated overnight and Wednesday. This 
saturated layer becomes deep enough for drizzle late tonight and 
Wednesday. The upper level low tracks northeast across Colorado 
Wednesday afternoon through Wednesday night bringing widespread 
rain and high country snow. The best snowfall for the mountains 
comes later Wednesday and Wednesday night when flow becomes a 
favorable northwest direction (for orographic lift). We've issued 
a Winter Weather Advisory for the mountains where 6 to 12 inches 
of snow are expected.The snow level tonight will be 10,000 to 
11,000 feet dipping below 10,000 feet over the northern mountains 
towards sunrise Wednesday morning. Once the low moves over 
Colorado, the snow level falls to 8,000 feet around sunset 
Wednesday evening and 7,500 feet by Thursday morning. Rain and 
snow linger into Thursday, especially across northern Colorado, 
wrapping up during the afternoon.

Skies clear out around sunset Thursday night as a surface settles
over Colorado. This will bring the coldest night so far this 
fall. Many places will see a frost or freeze Thursday night and 
Friday morning. Overnight lows are on track to be in the upper 20s
to mid 30s over northeast Colorado. Typical low lying areas/cold 
spots are expected to fall into the mid to lower 20s.

An upper level high will be centered over the intermountain west,
with a closed low trapped beneathit off the coast of northwest 
Mexico on Friday. Cross sections show a very dry airmass, 
resulting in sunny skies all day on Friday. Cool air lingers with 
highs in the upper 50s to lower 60s, but light winds and sunny 
skies will make it feel warmer. The upper level ridge slides east 
of the region Saturday. Southwestflow aloft will prevail behind 
the ridge bringing warmer air to the area. Temperatures climb 
above normal with highs expected to reach upper 60s to lower 70s 
across northeast Colorado.

A weak trough in the flow aloft tracks across the Central Rockies
on Sunday. It also absorbs the upper level low off the northwest 
Mexico coast. Models indicate very little moisture will accompany
this trough, thus dry conditions are expected to continue Sunday.
Temperatures may take a small step back.

Mild and dry conditions are expected for Monday andTuesday as
southwest flow redevelops over the Central Rockies ahead of a
deepening trough along the west coast. This trough tracks eastward
mid to late next week bringing the next chance for rain, mountain
snow, and cooler temperatures.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z TAFS through 18Z Wednesday/...
Issued at 1204 PM MDT Tue Oct 13 2026

Satellite shows the stratus deck is slowly breaking, with one
patch of brief clearing currently working southwest toward KDEN,
with a somewhat higher deck forming behind that near 2000-3000 ft
AGL. We should see a slow but continued breaking of the deck with
additional daytime heating, with mostly VFR conditions for a few 
hours late this afternoon and early evening. Then low clouds will 
settle in again and overspread the TAF sites, most likely 03Z-06Z 
and then lowering to IFR/LIFR with ceilings down to 500 ft or less
starting 06Z-08Z. These will hold through all day Wednesday. One 
batch of showers will attempt to move across the airports 23Z-04Z,
with more widespread showers and drizzle likely affecting KBJC 
after midnight. KDEN and KAPA would be more prone to the drizzle 
side through 16Z since moisture is quite shallow there. Showers 
will become more widespread across all TAF sites after 21Z 
Wednesday, with a low (10%) chance of thunder. 

&&

Winter Weather Advisory from noon Wednesday to 6 AM MDT Thursday 
for COZ031-033-034.
